0.headline: Runwal Enterprises trims IPO size by half, revises use of proceeds
0.heading: Runwal Enterprises trims IPO size by half, revises use of proceeds
0.intro: Runwal Enterprises IPO | The company will utilise Rs 100 crore of the net fresh issue proceeds to repay debt against its outstanding borrowings of Rs 431.4 crore on a standalone basis as of July 2026
0.body:
Mumbai-based real estate developer Runwal Enterprises has halved the size of its proposed public issue and accordingly revised the objectives of the offer.

The Subodh Runwal-promoted company had approached the capital markets in March 2025 by filing a draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to raise up to Rs 1,000 crore through an initial public offering (IPO). The issue comprised entirely of a fresh issue of shares.

The capital markets regulator subsequently approved the company's IPO papers in August 2025, clearing the way for the launch of the public issue.

According to a notice to investors dated September 10, Runwal Enterprises had filed an application with SEBI on August 11 seeking approval to reduce the issue size. The move follows new regulations that allow companies to increase or decrease their fresh issue size by up to 50 percent without refiling the DRHP.

Following SEBI's approval letter dated September 10, Runwal Enterprises has reduced the issue size to Rs 500 crore from the earlier Rs 1,000 crore and disclosed the change through an addendum dated September 11.

The company has also revised the objectives of the issue.

Runwal Enterprises will now utilise Rs 100 crore of the net fresh issue proceeds to repay debt against its outstanding borrowings of Rs 431.4 crore on a standalone basis as of July 2026.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

A further Rs 225 crore will be used for investment in its wholly owned material subsidiaries, Runwal Residency and Evie Real Estate, to repay a portion of their outstanding borrowings.

The total outstanding borrowings of Runwal Residency and Evie Real Estate stood at Rs 286.5 crore and Rs 356.4 crore, respectively, as of July 2026.

The remaining proceeds from the issue will be used to fund acquisitions of future real estate projects and for general corporate purposes.

Runwal Enterprises recorded consolidated sales value of Rs 2,353.5 crore in the financial year ended March 2026, an increase of 24 percent from Rs 1,899 crore in the previous year. However, its average selling price declined to Rs 11,366 per square foot during the period from Rs 11,754 per square foot a year earlier.

The company's total saleable area increased sharply to 2.07 million square feet in FY2026 from 1.62 million square feet in the previous year.

ICICI Securities and Jefferies India have been appointed as the merchant bankers managing the Runwal Enterprises IPO.

1.headline: Karamtara Engineering IPO subscription crosses 33x on Day 3 - Check GMP
1.heading: Karamtara Engineering IPO subscription crosses 33x on Day 3 - Check GMP
1.intro: Karamtara Engineering manufactures engineering steel products for the renewable energy and power transmission sectors.
1.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Karamtara Engineering was subscribed 33.12 times on Friday, the final day of bidding.

The Rs 875-crore IPO received bids for 84.18 crore shares against 2.54 crore shares on offer, according to data available till 3 pm.

The portion reserved for retail individual investors was subscribed 10.41 times, while the non-institutional investors' category was subscribed 37.42 times. The qualified institutional buyers' portion received bids for 70 times the shares on offer.

Karamtara Engineering, which manufactures engineering steel products for the renewable energy and power transmission sectors, had earlier raised Rs 262.50 crore from anchor investors.
Check All IPO News
Karamtara Engineering IPO GMP Today Price
According to platforms tracking the grey market activities, the shares of Karamtara Engineering are commanding a GMP of up to 26 percent. Investorgain quoted a GMP of Rs 65 for the shares of the company, indicating a listing gain of 25.6 percent.

The price band for the issue has been fixed at Rs 241-254 per share, valuing the company at around Rs 7,790-8,174 crore.

The company manufactures transmission line towers, solar structures and tracker components, wind energy structures, structural steel profiles and fasteners for domestic and overseas markets.

The shares are proposed to be listed on both the BSE and NSE on September 17.

2.headline: IPO-bound Fibe turns to merchant-led loans to reduce reliance on costly digital customer acquisition
2.heading: IPO-bound Fibe turns to merchant-led loans to reduce reliance on costly digital customer acquisition
2.intro: Fibe provides financing for hospital treatments, education fees, health insurance premiums, rooftop solar installations, travel and e-commerce purchases through its merchant network
2.body:
IPO-bound digital lender Fibe is increasingly sourcing borrowers through hospitals, educational institutions, insurers and other merchants, as it seeks to reduce its reliance on the costly digital acquisition of personal-loan customers, sources told Moneycontrol.

Social Worth Technologies, which operates Fibe, filed its draft red herring prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Board of India on June 29. The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to Rs 750 crore and an offer for sale of up to 4.01 crore shares by investors, including TPG-backed The Rise Fund III, Norwest Capital, Eight Roads Ventures and Piramal Finance. The total IPO size is likely to be around Rs 2,000 crore, the sources said.

Assets under management (AUM) in what Fibe calls its “purpose-driven financing” business more than tripled to Rs 1,946 crore in FY26 from Rs 581 crore in FY24, representing a compound annual growth rate of 83 percent, the draft documents show.

Its share of Fibe’s total AUM increased to 22.6 percent from 14.3 percent over the period, though personal loans continued to account for more than three-fourths of the loan book.

The so-called purpose-driven financing are loans that customers avail for specific end use cases like education or medical expenses.

Unlike personal loans, where customers are typically acquired through digital advertising, bureau-based targeting or existing relationships, purpose-driven loans are offered at the point of a transaction. Fibe provides financing for hospital treatments, education fees, health insurance premiums, rooftop solar installations, travel and e-commerce purchases through its merchant network.

The network expanded to 10,387 merchant touchpoints in FY26 from 3,294 in FY24. Annual disbursements through the segment rose to Rs 3,036 crore from Rs 953 crore, while its share of fresh disbursements increased to 36 percent from 26 percent. Since launching the business in 2021, Fibe has disbursed more than Rs 6,605 crore to 1.24 million customers.

Around 47.5 percent of Fibe’s new customers were acquired at zero customer-acquisition cost through the merchant-led channel in FY26, up from 24 percent two years earlier.

Fibe’s platform processed approximately 1.31 million loan applications a month, with 95 percent of loans decided through automated processing in FY26. Its credit scorecards use more than 27,500 variables, including bureau, income, demographic, device and behavioural information.

Fibe’s total AUM increased to Rs 8,603 crore in FY26 from Rs 4,064 crore in FY24, while profit after tax rose to Rs 291 crore from Rs 101 crore.
2.ai_impact_text_summary_s: IPO-bound digital lender Fibe is ditching costly digital acquisition. It now sources borrowers via hospitals, schools, and merchants for "purpose-driven financing," tripling AUM and cutting acquisition costs. This strategy precedes its Rs 2,000 crore IPO.
